shortDescription: European spot prices rose to more than one-week highs in early trading on Tuesday as German wind power supply was forecast to fall sharply.($1 = 0.8626 euros)

children: European spot prices rose to more than one-week highs in early trading on Tuesday as German wind power supply was forecast to fall sharply.
The German day-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBD1) rose 16.6% to €166.50 ($193.02) per megawatt-hour by 0910 GMT, its highest since August 20, LSEG data showed.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) rose 7.6% to €161.50/MWh, its highest since August 17, the data showed.
German wind power supply is expected to drop 10.4 gigawatts to 12.6 GW, while solar supply is seen down 460 megawatts at 15.3 GW, the data showed.
In France, fundamentals are seen mostly flat, with a 50 MW dip in wind supply.
European forward curve prices rose in early trading after strong gains on Monday, tracking a rise in gas prices above €70.
The German front-year baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) edged up 0.3% to €117.40/MWh, the data showed.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) gained 3.4% to €73/MWh.

Europe is heading into a winter with constrained gas supplies and low storage levels, which should push gas and power prices higher but fall short of the levels reached during the 2022 crisis, Morningstar said.

U.S. President Donald Trump threatened further strikes against Iran on Monday after the first exchange of direct attacks in a month, raising tensions in a conflict that had recently shifted into an economic standoff.
